chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, from Humran ibn A'yan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed Jibra'il عليه السلام came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله with two pomegranates. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله ate one of them, and he broke the other into two halves. He ate one half and fed Ali half. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “O my brother, do you know what these two pomegranates are?” He said: “No.” He said: “As for the first, it is prophethood; you have no share in it. And as for the other, it is knowledge; you are my partner in it.”

So I said: “May Allah keep you well, how was he his partner in it?” He said: “Allah did not teach Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله any knowledge except that He commanded him to teach it to Ali عليه السلام.”

key_terms.الرُّمَّانَتَانِ: the two pomegranates, symbolic of prophethood and knowledge
key_terms.النُّبُوَّةُ: prophethood, a station specifically denied here to Imam Ali عليه السلام
key_terms.الْعِلْمُ: divinely taught knowledge shared with Imam Ali عليه السلام
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلَ: Jibra'il عليه السلام, the angelic messenger who brought the symbolic gift
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, recipient of revelation and divine knowledge
key_terms.شَرِيكِي: my partner, indicating participation in the Prophet’s knowledge
key_terms.عَلِيًّا: Imam Ali عليه السلام, designated as the Prophet’s partner in knowledge

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe Imam Ali’s partnership with the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله in knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Jibra'il عليه السلام brought two pomegranates to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, one symbolizing prophethood and the other knowledge. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله clarified that Imam Ali عليه السلام had no share in prophethood, but was his partner in knowledge, and that every knowledge taught to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was also commanded to be taught to Ali عليه السلام. The narration highlights the unique rank of Imam Ali عليه السلام in receiving the prophetic inheritance of divinely taught knowledge.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman, from Humran Bin Ayn, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> came to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> with two pomegranates. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> ate one of the two and broke the other one in two halves. So he<sup>saww</sup> ate half and fed Ali<sup>asws</sup> half. Then Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O my<sup>saww</sup> brother<sup>asws</sup>! Do you<sup>asws</sup> know what there two pomegranates are?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘As for the first, so it is the Prophet-hood. There isn’t a share for you<sup>asws</sup> in it. And as for the other, so it is the knowledge. You<sup>asws</sup> are my<sup>saww</sup> associate in it’.

So I said, ‘May Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Keep you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> well! He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> happened to be his<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> associate in it?’ He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> did not Teach Muhammad<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> a knowledge except that He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Commanded him<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> that he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> teaches it to Ali<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn ’Udhayna from ‘Abdallah ibn Sulayman from Humran ibn A‘yan from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Once Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah and brought him two pieces of pomegranates. The Messenger of Allah ate one of them and broke the other one into two pieces. He then ate one half and fed the other half to Ali (a.s.). The Messenger of Allah said, “O my brother, do you know what those pieces of pomegranates were?” He said, “No, I do not know.” He then said, “The first one was prophet-hood. There is no share in it for you. The other one is knowledge in which you’re my partner.”
I then said, “May Allah keep you well, how was that?” He would be his partner in it?” He said, “Allah did not teach any knowledge but that He commanded him to teach it to Ali (a.s.).”
